questions.answer: `json=` serializes dict to JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json. `data=` sends form-encoded (application/x-www-form-urlencoded). Use json= for REST JSON APIs, data= for HTML login forms.
questions.question: When do you use `json=` vs `data=` in requests?

questions.answer: `params={...}` auto-builds and encodes the query string (?page=2&limit=10); avoids manual string bugs with spaces/special chars. `headers={...}` sends metadata like Accept and Authorization Bearer tokens.
questions.question: What do `params=` and `headers=` do?

questions.answer: status_code (200/404), json() parsed dict, text raw string, headers metadata, url final URL, ok True if <400. Wrap in try/except: raise_for_status() raises HTTPError on 4xx/5xx; catch Timeout and RequestException parent.
